newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: BHP Petr sees 3 pct rise in liquids output.
newsitem.headline: BHP Petr sees 3 pct rise in liquids output.

text.p: The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd's BHP Petroleum unit said it expected its liquids production to rise by about three percent in the year to May 31, 1998, and its natural gas output to rise about two percent.

"Liquids production for fiscal 1998 is expected to increase by approximately three percent compared with fiscal 1997, with Liverpool Bay reaching plateau production during the year, offset to some extent by a possible shutdown at Wanaea-Cossack for repairs to the gas export system," BHP Petroleum executive general maanager John O'Connor told a media briefing.
He said natural field decline in Bass Strait was expected to be offset by a full year's production from the West Tuna and Bream B fields and a continuation of infill drilling in Bass Strait.
Gas output was expected to be marginally higher in fiscal 1998 with Liverpool Bay also producing at plateau rates for the full year, O'Connor said.

In its 1996/97 year ended May 31, BHP produced 68.95 million barrels of crude oil and condensate, up marginally from 68.50 million the previous year, and 247.1 billion cubic feet of gas, down from 263.1 billion.

When asked about the Wanaea-Cossack gas/liquids project offshore Western Australia, O'Connor told Reuters that BHP expected the project's operator to undertake repair work to the export system within the next 12 months.
"We think it should be taken down and looked at," O'Connor said.
"Hopefully, that would increase capacity," he added.
Woodside Petroleum Ltd is the operator of Wanaea-Cossack.
The project has been forced to reduce production rates several times by problems with the gas export system.
